title: ～という (〜to iu) Noun
shortExplanation: Used to define or explain a noun more specifically.
longExplanation: The ～という grammar point is used to define or explain a noun more specifically. It is often translated as 'called', 'named', or 'that is to say' in English. It can be used with nouns, な-adjectives, and adjectival verbs.
formation: Noun + という + Noun, な-Adjective + という + Noun, Adjectival Verb + という + Noun

examples.jp: 彼は日本語が流暢なアメリカ人という人です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa nihongo ga ryuuchou na amerikajin to iu hito desu.
examples.en: He is an American who speaks fluent Japanese.

examples.jp: 昨日、美味しかったというケーキを食べました。
examples.romaji: Kinou, oishikatta to iu keeki wo tabemashita.
examples.en: Yesterday, I ate a cake that was said to be delicious.

examples.jp: 有名な歌手という彼女は、たくさんのファンがいます。
examples.romaji: Yuumei na kashu to iu kanojo wa, takusan no fan ga imasu.
examples.en: She, who is called a famous singer, has many fans.

examples.jp: 環境に優しいという製品が人気があります。
examples.romaji: Kankyou ni yasashii to iu seihin ga ninki ga arimasu.
examples.en: Products that are said to be environmentally friendly are popular.
